findings.summary: The guide and the verifier header state a refuted git fact: a forged commit-graph 'fools git log and git rev-list but not merge-base --is-ancestor'. It DOES fool merge-base --is-ancestor when an INTERIOR commit is forged.
findings.detail: Reviewer fixture (git 2.53.0, generationVersion 1 and 2): local c1<-c3, remote c1<-c2a<-c2; commit-graph written, c2a's CDAT parent patched to c3 (topo level 3, GDA2 offset raised, checksum recomputed). Plain `git merge-base --is-ancestor c3 c2` rc=0 (fooled), with -c core.commitGraph=false rc=1. Current verifier exits 12 (DIVERGED, correct). A scratch copy of the verifier with only ` -c core.commitGraph=false` removed exits 0 (false clean) on the same repo, so the class was a real PASS-bluff before round 10, not 'no false pass shown'. The r2 reviewer and the guide only forged the TIP commit, which git parses from the object (command-line arguments), so the tip variant is not fooled. Wrong statements: verify_repos.sh header lines 73-74; docs/scripts/verify_repos.md line 160 ('fools git log and git rev-list but not git merge-base --is-ancestor') and line 170 ('was not fooled ... so no false pass was shown'). The source fix itself is correct and stays.

findings.summary: R2/N1 not class-complete: a repository-level core.excludesFile set through include.path, includeIf or config.worktree is treated as 'global' and hides untracked work: exit 0 (false clean).
findings.detail: Line 178 reads `git config --local --get core.excludesFile`; --local reads .git/config only and does not follow includes (git default for a named file) nor config.worktree. Fixtures: (a) .git/config include.path=inc.cfg with core.excludesFile=.git/myexcl listing u, untracked u: `git config --show-scope` says local, verifier rc=0 dirty_untracked=0; (b) extensions.worktreeConfig + `git config --worktree core.excludesFile`: scope worktree, rc=0; (c) includeIf.gitdir: rc=0. A direct `git config core.excludesFile` (no include) is caught (rc=13, named). Candidate fix: decide 'local' by `git config --show-scope --get core.excludesFile` (scopes local, worktree, command), add the three fixtures. The header/guide claim 'a REPOSITORY-level core.excludesFile' is covered is inaccurate until then.

findings.summary: Direct execution (the path the guide recommends) still exports a caller BASH_ENV/ENV to every child: a bash-script git shim/wrapper sourced it 21 times in one run; only the interpreter path (`bash verify_repos.sh`) unsets it.
findings.detail: Line 83 unsets BASH_ENV/ENV only inside the re-exec branch. Measured with a recording `#!/bin/bash` (no -p) VERIFY_GIT shim on a 1-repo --no-remote run: direct exec canary=21, shim calls seeing BASH_ENV=21; `bash -p verify_repos.sh` also 21; `bash verify_repos.sh` canary=1 (bash startup, unavoidable), children 0. The verifier's own -p processes do not source it (bash -p -c probe: 0; exported functions and SHELLOPTS/PS4 also blocked by -p, measured). Doc line 172 ('so no child sees the caller's BASH_ENV ... execute the file directly') is therefore wrong for the direct path. Fix: `unset BASH_ENV ENV` unconditionally right after line 83; r9 N3 tests only the interpreter path and uses a `#!/bin/bash -p` shim that cannot source it, add a direct-exec case with a non-p shim.
